newsitem.title: FRANCE: French farmers seen boosting winter wheat sowings.
newsitem.headline: French farmers seen boosting winter wheat sowings.

text.p: French farmers are poised to plant more winter wheat in a bid to expand on this year's record harvest, industry officials said on Monday.
No official sowing estimates are available, but already seed manufacturers are reporting growth in sales this year.

"Depending on which region, sales of seed for soft wheat were five or 10 percent higher this autumn," an official at the semi-public National Seeding and Planting Group (GNIS), which monitors the seed industry, told Reuters.
Farmers have scope to sow more grain after the European Union halved its set-aside rate to five percent for the 1997 crop.
And the relative firmness of local wheat prices, despite a recent fall on international markets, has preserved the incentive to sow, farm officials said.

Farm ministry figures published last week indicate farmers increased their sowings of soft winter wheat last autumn by six percent. The winter-sown area was 4.74 million hectares out of a total 4.77 million ha, the farm ministry said.
Winter wheat output was 34.42 million tonnes out of a total 34.57 million tonnes, a record.
Officials caution against extrapolating the area sown directly from patterns in the sale of seed.
Much depends on the use of seed grown on farm and held back from the crop sent to market. In France 46 percent of soft wheat seed is grown directly on farm or 30 percent for barley.
Purchases of manufactured seed show a trend, but there is no fixed link with sowings, the GNIS official said.
"Five or 10 percent (increase in seed sales) doesn't mean the area will go up by the same amount," he said.
Production is even more at the mercy of unknown factors such as the weather's impact on yields.
But others agreed the trend for soft wheat sowings seemed to be upwards this year, while rapeseed was stabilising after gaining ground last year.
"There will be a small rise for rapeseed --nothing spectacular," said a grain authority official in central France, the country's principal grain region.
Soft wheat would be up by an unspecified amount, he said.
Soft wheat sowings are just starting there, while rapeseed and barley have finished. No barley figures were available.
Also in central France, recently sown rapeseed is said to be well established after rain in late September, which washed away the effects of mid-year drought.
The same weather has created ideal conditions for sowing soft wheat, the local grain official said.
Winter wheat sowing is well advanced in southern France and yet to get going in the north, other officials said.
Total sowings are usually complete by November 15.
Officials at the French wheat farmers' association, the AGPB, said winter soft wheat sowings was set for an increase in area this year but it was too early to be precise.
